source_ref: Li J, Wu N, Xiong S (2021) 'Sustainable innovation in the context of organizational cultural diversity: The role of cultural intelligence and knowledge sharing', PLoS ONE 16(5):e0250878, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0250878 (CC BY 4.0). TEXT: S1 Appendix 'Questionnaire' (.s001, DOCX), section headed 'Cultural Intelligence（CQ）', items numbered 1-12. DATA: S1 File (.s002, XLS) with bare headers ID/SEX/.../CQ1..CQ12/... . S2 File (.s003, DOCX) gives per-item min/max/mean/SD. Instrument: 12-item CQS short form of Bucker, Furrer & Lin, derived from Ang et al. (2007) 20-item CQS. Processing script data/li_2021_cultural_intelligence.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/li_2021_cultural_intelligence/.
note: MAPPING (paper_explicit). data/li_2021_cultural_intelligence.py melts BY NAME ([c for c in df.columns if c.startswith('CQ')]) from the S1 File workbook, so the IRW code IS the source column name -- no positional step, no rename (core model s3, pattern 1). But the workbook carries only bare headers (it is an .xls with no variable or value labels), so the tie from column CQ1..CQ12 to wording comes from S1 Appendix, which prints the 12 items under a section header naming the code prefix ('Cultural Intelligence（CQ）') and numbers them 1-12 in the canonical CQS facet order. CHECKED AGAINST THE DATA, re-runnable as verify_li_2021_cultural_intelligence.R: route 5, the four-facet block the shipped text implies (metacognitive CQ1-2, cognitive CQ3-7, motivational CQ8-9, behavioural CQ10-12) is the strongest block for 12/12 items (e.g. CQ1 own 0.81 vs best rival 0.54; CQ7 own 0.61 vs 0.48); route 8, the five knowledge items are exactly the five lowest means in the table (CQ7 4.09, CQ6 4.11, CQ3 4.16, CQ4 4.27, CQ5 4.37 against 4.68-5.21 for the other seven). PARTIAL, not VERIFIED: neither route separates items WITHIN a block -- CQ1 vs CQ2 correlate 0.81, and CQ3/CQ6/CQ7 means (4.16/4.11/4.09) are within 0.07 of each other -- so order inside each facet rests on the S1 Appendix listing alone. The S2 File's per-item means reproduce the S1 File exactly (CQ1 5.21/1.175 etc.) but that is the same data and was NOT used as independent evidence. TEXT: transcribed verbatim from S1 Appendix, including its own punctuation ('I know the rules (e.g. vocabulary, grammar) of other languages.'); the leading '1.'-'12.' numbering was stripped. option_text is BLANK for all 84 rows: the questionnaire prints the scale as unlabelled checkboxes '1□ 2□ 3□ 4□ 5□ 6□ 7□' and the paper says only 'a Likert 7-point scale', so no anchors exist in any source and the points were not padded with their own numbers. instructions is the questionnaire's own opening paragraph, which frames the whole form (all four scales); section_prompt is blank and there is a single trivial section_id. correct_response empty (attitude scale, no key). LANGUAGE: administered to Chinese employees in 31 Chinese enterprises, partly via 'Questionnaire Star' (a Chinese survey platform), by authors at Zhongnan University of Economics and Law, so the administration was in Chinese; the paper never states this explicitly, which is why it is recorded here rather than asserted as quoted. The administered Chinese wording is NOT recoverable within the deposit or the paper's own supplements: S1 Appendix contains zero Chinese characters in its document body (the 1,488 CJK characters in the .docx are font and style names -- 宋体, 楷体, 华文行楷 -- in document.xml, styles.xml, theme1.xml and fontTable.xml only), the S1 File .xls has zero CJK in headers or cells, and S2 File is a statistics table. So the documented fallback applies: the study's own English questionnaire ships in the base fields, the _translated columns are empty, and language=Chinese is retained as the signal. translation_source=study_supplied -- the English is the authors' own S1 Appendix, nothing was translated by this project. STEP 3b, clean: the live table is 12 items on 1-7, matching the paper's 'The scale has 12 items and uses a Likert 7-point scale' and the S1 Appendix's 12 CQ items; both sample items the paper quotes ('I vary the rate of my speaking when a cross-cultural situation requires it') appear in the shipped text. The deposit's other three scales (SIB1-6, KS1-4, OCD1-9) are separate IRW tables and were not touched. Several unrelated li_* tables exist in the corpus; this one was confirmed against its own processing script's DOI. RIGHTS: no restriction to quote. The CQS is not fee-licensed and no redistribution bar from Ang et al. or Bucker et al. was found; the wording actually copied here comes from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS article's own supplement, which governs under the ECR-R ruling.
public_note: The questionnaire was administered to employees in Chinese enterprises, but the study's deposit publishes only an English version of it (S1 Appendix contains no Chinese text at all), so the item text shown is the authors' own English wording and is not what respondents read. The 1-7 response options carry no text because no source labels them: the questionnaire prints seven unlabelled checkboxes and the paper says only that a 7-point Likert scale was used

source_ref: Li J, Wu N, Xiong S (2021) 'Sustainable innovation in the context of organizational cultural diversity: The role of cultural intelligence and knowledge sharing', PLOS ONE 16(5):e0250878, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0250878 (CC BY 4.0) -- S1 Appendix 'Questionnaire' (.s001, DOCX), 'Knowledge Sharing（KS）' block, items 1-4, for the item text and the unlabelled 7-point response scale; Measures section for the instrument attribution and 'Likert 7-point scale'; Table 2 (t002, read as an image) for the per-item CFA loadings used in verification; S2 File response workbook (.s002, WPS .xls) for the KS1-KS4 column headers; processing script data/li_2021_cultural_intelligence.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/li_2021_knowledge_sharing/.
note: MAPPING paper_explicit. The S1 Appendix questionnaire (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0250878.s001, DOCX, read with python-docx) heads its third block 'Knowledge Sharing（KS）' and numbers exactly four items 1-4; the S2 data workbook's header holds KS1..KS4 in that block, so the section's own code plus its item numbering ties each sentence to a column (explicit code-label match). CODE DERIVATION is pattern 1, nothing to get wrong: data/li_2021_cultural_intelligence.py selects [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith('KS')] and melts with var_name='item', so the IRW item code IS the S2 column name -- no rename, no positional step. LEVEL-1 CHECKED AND ABSENT: the .s002 workbook is a bare WPS .xls with one sheet, 41 header cells and no variable or value labels of any kind, so the appendix is the highest available source. STRUCTURAL CORROBORATION across the whole file: the appendix's four instrument blocks give 12 / 4 / 4+5 / 6 numbered items and the S2 header gives exactly CQ1-12, KS1-4, OCD1-9, SIB1-6 (41 columns = ID + 9 covariates + 31 items), so every block's count and code prefix reconcile. VERIFICATION (route 1, verify_li_2021_knowledge_sharing.R): a one-factor CFA on the live data reproduces the paper's Table 2 standardized loadings to 0.0004 and their SEs to 0.0005 (KS1 0.794/0.024, KS2 0.820/0.022, KS3 0.880/0.018, KS4 0.827/0.021 observed vs 0.794/0.024, 0.820/0.022, 0.880/0.018, 0.827/0.022 published); Table 2 is an image, the numbers are not in the article text. PARTIAL because the rival sweep scores the KS2<->KS4 swap at 0.0074, inside tolerance, so those two are not separated, and the appendix-numbering link is a label match rather than a data test (live item means span only 0.31: 4.83/5.07/5.14/4.93). STEP 3B: no instrument mismatch -- 4 items on 1-7 with n=336 each matches the paper's 336 valid questionnaires and its 'questionnaire contains 4 items' for KS, and the item content is knowledge sharing, not the siblings' cultural intelligence (CQ1-12), organizational culture differences (OCD1-9) or sustainable innovation behaviour (SIB1-6). DEVIATIONS: leading item numbering ('1.') stripped from each appendix line, each stripped number asserted equal to the code's numeric suffix first; instructions holds the S1 Appendix cover page verbatim, its Word line breaks joined into one paragraph (whole-questionnaire framing, shared with the three sibling tables from the same appendix; the KS block has no instruction line of its own); option_text blank at all seven levels because the appendix prints unlabelled boxes. LANGUAGE: administered in Chinese -- INFERRED, not stated: the paper never names an administration language nor says the appendix is a translation, but the sample is Chinese employees of 31 Chinese enterprises surveyed by mailed paper forms, e-mail and the Chinese 'Questionnaire Star' (wenjuanxing) platform, and the .s002 workbook's OLE metadata reads Locale ID 2052 (zh-CN), creating application WPS; no Chinese wording exists in either supplement (S1 Appendix is entirely English; S2 holds only integers and English headers), so the 2026-09-01 fallback applies and the English is the authors' own. RIGHTS: the PLOS ONE article and both supplements are CC BY 4.0, and the wording was copied from the CC BY supplement; no fee, non-commercial or no-redistribution clause could be found or quoted for the source scale (Faraj & Sproull 2000, as applied by Srivastava, Bartol & Locke 2006), so under the 2026-09-04 quote test silence is permission. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict, table shipped.
public_note: The survey was fielded to employees of Chinese enterprises and was in all likelihood administered in Chinese -- the paper does not state the language, and the inference rests on the Chinese sample and the data workbook's own locale metadata, but the only questionnaire published in the study's supplements is in English, so the item text shown here is the authors' own English rendering rather than the wording respondents read; the seven scale points are printed as unlabelled boxes in that questionnaire and the paper describes them only as a 7-point Likert scale, so no response-option text is available
